title: Auto crease rings and the crease overlay: seed crease rings at the crease field's maxima (auto-rings, Ctrl+U), score them against IMG_4111's hand rings, and show the field and its maxima over any look
user-messages: ok archive view-29 and add those to craw-102
description:
Experiment. Segmentation agents spent most of their time on a screenshot, guess a pixel, pick-scan, click loop to find grooves (ai-workspace reports/tool-review-2026-11-06.md, items 1, 3, 5). Test whether grooves alone find the boundaries the user drew.

1. Seeds: from SurfaceCreases.valleyStrength, keep vertices above a threshold that are maximal ACROSS the groove (a groove is a line, so point maxima along it are noise), giving thin valley lines; group connected valley-line vertices into curves; drop short curves; one seed per curve at its strongest vertex.
2. Rings: at each seed, do what the ring tool's hover preview does (ClosedRingTool: GirdlingPlane at the vertex, then a one-anchor trace in crease mode). Keep rings that close and are simple, drop body-wide rings over a maximum length, drop duplicates (several seeds on one groove).
3. Output: the survivors as spline_ring statements (mode="crease", one anchor plus normal, the same form RingDslWriter writes) appended to a copy of a scan's DSL, so the ring scene loads them like any segmentation.
4. Scoring on IMG_4111 (the user's hand-segmented reference, dsl/crawfish/IMG_4111.dsl): for each hand ring, the nearest generated ring by mean polyline distance; recall = share of hand rings matched within a tolerance, false positives = generated rings matching none; region and sliver counts. Compare with the ring_candidates node (skeleton necks) as a baseline.

Run it inside the ring scene as an automation route plus ixdar-cli command (e.g. auto-rings --threshold --max-length --out), because a crawfish scene is about 1M faces and runs on the Mac Studio scene host. Parameters are explored, not fixed: report how recall and false positives move with threshold and minimum curve length.

Added 2026-11-07, user: "ok archive view-29 and add those to craw-102".

Ctrl+U (built, uncommitted): the ring tool's Ctrl+U rings every local maximum of the crease field with the sweep's best setting, as unsaved one-anchor crease rings in one undoable edit; a ring repeating a live wall is dropped. Rings loaded from the DSL and not adopted are not yet checked as repeats.

Crease overlay (from the archived VIEW-29, written 2026-10-25): see where the grooves are while placing rings and naming parts, for the user and for agents reading screenshots. It replaces VIEW-22's crease heat map, which the user did not like.
1. Data: one per-vertex value, valley strength over the field's saturation (0 to 1, SurfaceCreases.valleyCurvature / saturation), the same scale as CreaseValleySeeds' threshold, so the darkest bands are where Ctrl+U finds rings. From the one shared crease lookup (RingTool.readyCreases); nothing built twice, uploaded once per surface.
2. Drawing: mesh.fs (the one lit shader since VIEW-31) applies it after the base colour, whatever the base is (region colours, part colours, the plain surface, any look), so creases read as darker bands and the colouring underneath stays readable; it never replaces the colouring. Strength mapped through a named Palettes ramp or a single named Color (no colour arithmetic in Java). It needs a per-vertex slot of its own: VIEW-31's field slot (attribute 3) belongs to field looks such as split_density, and the overlay must work over any look.
3. Control: a toggle row with a stable action id and an explicit key in the ring tool and the region tool (listed by `tools`, fired by `control`).
4. Agents: a way to turn it on for a capture, e.g. `ixdar-cli multiview --creases`, and its state in ui-state.

Crease-field maxima dots, shown with the overlay:
5. Every local maximum CreaseValleySeeds finds as a dot that the surface hides like the ring anchors (MeshOverlayRuntime's discs); maxima joined into one groove curve share a colour, and each curve's seed (where a Ctrl+U ring starts) is drawn larger.
6. CreaseValleySeeds keeps which curve each maximum belongs to (today it only counts curves) so the dots can be coloured by curve.
7. The ring tool already uploads its anchors through the overlay's one disc buffer, so the maxima need a buffer of their own or a merged upload; neither may hide the other.
definition-of-done:
1. An automation route and ixdar-cli command produce the generated-ring DSL for a loaded scan, with seed, ring and rejection counts in the reply.
2. A unit test on a small synthetic mesh with known grooves (e.g. a capsule with two circumferential grooves) finds one ring per groove and none elsewhere.
3. IMG_4111 scored: recall, false positives, region and sliver counts for at least three threshold settings, against the hand rings and against ring_candidates, written to the ticket and to tmp/auto-rings-report.md.
4. A multiview with region colours of the best setting on IMG_4111, and the same setting run on one unsegmented scan (IMG_4114), in tmp/; a launch entry opens the IMG_4111 result in the ring scene.
5. No change to the hand-segmented DSLs under dsl/crawfish/; generated DSLs live under tmp/ or a clearly named experiment file.

6. Ctrl+U in the ring tool adds the crease rings to the open scene as one undoable unsaved edit; a launch entry opens a blank scan to press it on.
7. The crease overlay shows over region colours, part colours and the plain surface on IMG_4111 and fertility, creases visibly darker; screenshots on and off. Toggling it changes nothing else (region colours, labels, picks identical).
8. No second crease build: the overlay's values come from the shared crease lookup (a test), and the toggle has a test.
9. The maxima dots show with the overlay, coloured by curve with each seed larger, without hiding or being hidden by the ring tool's anchors; a test that CreaseValleySeeds reports each maximum's curve.
10. `ixdar-cli multiview --creases` (or the chosen spelling) captures with the overlay and dots on, and ui-state reports whether they are on.
testing-plan:
1. The synthetic-groove unit test.
2. The IMG_4111 scoring run on the Mac scene host, numbers in the report.
3. The user looks at the multiviews.

4. Overlay and maxima on IMG_4111 and fertility on the Mac scene host: multiviews with it on and off over default, regions and parts.
5. The user presses Ctrl+U on a blank scan and toggles the overlay.
changes-made: Added auto-rings route and ixdar-cli command (CreaseValleySeeds, AutoCreaseRings, AutoRingScore, AutoRingDslWriter, AutoRings) with AutoCreaseRingsTest. IMG_4111 best setting (threshold 0.85, min_length 0.05, max_length 0.6, duplicate 0.02): 45 rings, 28/38 hand rings and 32/56 bisectors within 0.02 of the diagonal, 9 of 45 rings unmatched, 160 regions/130 slivers (hand 98/8); ring_candidates baseline: 3 rings, 3/94 walls matched. Sliver-free variant: 0 slivers, about half the recall. Six other scans scored against the agents' DSLs. Full tables: tmp/auto-rings-report.md in the craw-102 worktree.

Follow-up: seeding replaced by local maxima of valley strength within a radius (flag, default 0.008 of the diagonal), joined into curves by widest path, one ring per curve, rings merged when they lie along a kept ring (merge_close/merge_share). IMG_4111 best new setting (radius 0.008, merge 0.015/0.05, max_length 0.6): 91 rings, 29/38 hand rings and 29/56 bisectors within 0.02, 52 rings match no hand wall, 86 regions / 23 slivers (first run: 45 rings, 28/38, 32/56, 9 unmatched, 160/130). Six agent scans re-scored with first-run comparison; launch entries 'CRAW-102: IMG_411x auto-maxima' open each result (checked). Tables: tmp/auto-rings-report.md in the craw-102 worktree.

Crease overlay: V in the ring scene (every tool, action toggle-creases) darkens the surface toward the palette's new crease colour by the ring tool's shared valley strength (mesh.vs/mesh.fs attribute 4, HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.setCreaseStrength), over any look; CreaseOverlay uploads once per surface. Maxima dots on their own disc buffer in MeshOverlayRuntime, drawn before the anchors, coloured by curve, seeds larger. CreaseValleySeeds records maximumVertexIds/maximumCurves/maximumSeeds and now requires a maximum to beat its one-ring (fertility: 7391 -> 67 maxima). AutoRingSettings.seeder shared by Ctrl+U and the dots. multiview --creases; ui-state creaseOverlay {shown, uploaded, maxima, curves}. PatchColoursTest pointed at mesh.fs (VIEW-31 left it on the deleted mesh_scalar.fs).

Crease strength is now a 'creases' field look (no mesh-shader special case); V steps the maxima dots none / all / saddles only (convex along the groove, from the crease build's other principal curvature), and Ctrl+U rings the set V shows. IMG_4111 from 94 rings: all 983 maxima / 434 curves -> 45 rings in 12.6 s; saddles 526 / 320 -> 44 rings in 9.9 s. Every surface dot (ring anchors, connection picks, crease maxima, diagnostics, patch clouds, quad-layout corners, singularities, graph and T-mesh nodes) now goes through one MeshOverlayRuntime.setDots layer API drawing SurfaceDots as screen-space discs; PointSet spheres and the sphere-radius caps are gone.

V gains a fourth step, candidates (CreaseCandidates): every vertex whose unclamped valley curvature is positive and beats each direct neighbour, ties to the higher id, dotted by rank on the palette's scalar ramp, strongest brightest; no radius, threshold or cut. IMG_4113: 4660 candidates; top ranks line the tail-segment joints and the underside's curved grooves, plate noise ranks low; the broad outer U-groove on the underside carries almost none. ui-state creaseOverlay.candidates; multiview --creases candidates. Captures tmp/craw-102-4113-abd-candidates.png (creases look) and -clay.png. Tests: AutoCreaseRingsTest.candidatesBeatEveryNeighbourStrongestFirst, CreaseOverlayTest V cycle.

Converging-ring proposer (ConvergingCreaseRings, SeedRing): from each candidate (strongest first) the hover's one-anchor crease ring is traced, then re-traced from the strongest vertex on it (its snapped edge loop), until a ring's strongest vertex is the vertex it was traced from; that ring reproduces itself and is proposed at that vertex. Chains reaching a proposed ring support it; failing or cycling chains propose nothing; each vertex traced at most once. Rings are the same only when they mark the same edges: no distance, strength or count cut. V gains a fifth step, proposals: one trace a frame, each ring's point large and its supporters small in its colour; hovering a point previews its ring, a click adds exactly that ring. Ctrl+U now adds the next proposal no live ring already marks (one undoable ring a press) instead of the sweep's batch. Candidate dots use the ramp's visible stops; hover shows a candidate's rank and strength. Route/CLI converge-rings runs it to the end and reports chain fates and trace outcomes. SeedRing is the one-seed trace AutoCreaseRings now shares. Test: AutoCreaseRingsTest.theGroovesAreTheRingsTheCandidatesConvergeTo (both tube grooves proposed once, each a fixed point).

IMG_4113 converge-rings run (blank scan, 964k faces, 127 s): 4660 candidates, 6499 traces; chains: 944 found a ring that reproduces itself, 2993 joined one, 110 cycled, 613 failed (208 not traced, 37 crossing, 32 no single edge loop, 23 unwritable). 581 of the 944 proposals are supported only by their own candidate, mostly tiny rings round plate bumps (median length 0.04 of the diagonal); the 75 with 10 or more supporters have median length 0.125 and sit on the grooves. Discovery order mixes them (proposals 2-5 are singles), so support is the better ranking. Captures tmp/craw-102-4113-abd-proposals.png and -clay.png; report tmp/converge-4113.json.

Crease path looks: CreaseLoopField traces the hover's crease path (sheet Dijkstra, no spline fit) at every vertex on worker threads; ring scene looks crease-path-length and crease-path-group (each vertex coloured by the attractor its strongest-vertex pointers reach). IMG_4113: 482219 vertices in 166 s, 481626 with a path. Geodesic cache in SurfaceGeodesics (exact; 32% of geodesics remembered, run time unchanged within noise).
